issues.title: C. Create orders component
issues.body:
Use table component to display list of messages.  A _placeholder_ for this has been created as `Planning-Messages-List`.

Suggest this component: https://github.com/mbrn/material-table

Props (all from state):
* channel id (to be used when sending new message)
* messages for this channel (duh)
* player role (to be used when sending new message)
* player force (to filter messages)
* isUmpire (if true, include drop-down at top of channel to choose `view-as` force)
* templates for this wargame (used to render message _detail_, and for creating new messages).

Component will run "map" on messages to produced reduced array suitable for rendering.  The reduce function will extract the fields displayed below.

Display one row per message, initially (*) with these headers:
* id
* title
* from-role
* status
* start date
* finish date

(*) Users to provide exact fields in early Sept.

Page should have `sort` on id, title, start-date, finish-date. Page should have `filter` on `status`.

It should be possible for players to expand messages, to read the detail (presented using the JSON-Editor with the relevant template - like how we did for `COA Status Board`).

Have mocked up how a player may view their orders here:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1108513/187191841-8059b2f6-f16a-4c78-a180-8c5ea84b972f.png)

issues.title: D. Create PlanningAssets component
issues.body:
Create a component that shows a table of assets.

A `renderer` method (passed in as prop) will take an `Asset` object and return a `string[]` of table cells.

Props (all from state):
* ForceData[] (source data)
* PlayerForce - display data for that force
* isUmpire - if true, included drop-down for umpire to choose `view-as` force

The component should receive a `forces` object, `player-force` value and `renderer` method in `props`.

If `player-force` is provided, only show assets of that force.  If no `player-force` provided, show all assets.  The renderer method will either return the real values (when looking at own force) or `perceived` values (when looking at other forces).

Use this table component:
https://github.com/mbrn/material-table

Where an asset `comprises` other assets, the `children` assets should be grouped beneath the parent.

Test data is present in `p9.mock.ts`, developed in support of #1745 

Have attempted to mockup of how a player may see "own" and "other" assets:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1108513/187191691-dcdf8088-3fb3-4255-8824-caf8ef2c8a90.png)

issues.title: Refactor NewMessage to be component based
issues.body:
We currently only use `<NewMessage/>` from the `client` package, where it is stored.

But, I need to access it from the `components` package. So, we should refactor it to match the structure of our `components`, and create a story/spec to test it.

If possible, we should refactor `MessageCreator` to the new `Component` model at the same time.

It looks like both elements are already TypeScript, we just need to match our new way of building things.

We could (temporarily) call the new version `<NewMessage2/>` during testing. Once it's accepted, we drop the existing `NewMessage` and rename `NewMessage2` to `NewMessage`.
